summary: Strengthen network troubleshooting, change control and reporting skills. Explore this five-day intermediate network administration course.
lede: Computer network administration covers maintaining and troubleshooting LAN and WAN services through TCP/IP diagnostics, monitoring, and controlled configuration changes. For network administrators, NOC analysts, and infrastructure engineers, the course builds skills in documenting network baselines, interpreting SNMP and Syslog indicators, tracing connectivity and DNS or DHCP faults, and assessing VLAN and routing changes.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course suits professionals who already work with network services and need a more consistent method for keeping them available, diagnosing faults and controlling configuration changes.
prerequisites: Working knowledge of TCP/IP, basic IPv4 addressing and routine network support tasks. Programming is not required. Advanced monitoring automation and packet-analysis methods are introduced conceptually; the course does not require implementation or coding.
